sa-oryctolagus-cuniculus.title: Rabbit
sa-oryctolagus-cuniculus.summary: Smart, social and long-lived, rabbits are a big commitment, often as long as a dog. They need a bonded rabbit companion, lots of room to run, unlimited hay and things to chew.
rows: Varies greatly by breed, from small dwarf breeds to the Flemish Giant

Indoors: at least an 8 sq ft pen as a home base plus a rabbit-proofed room to run in for several hours a day. For two rabbits, a combined shelter and exercise area of at least 3 × 2 m and 1 m high (about 10 × 6.5 × 3 ft) is recommended. No wire floors. Litter box

About 85% hay or grass (unlimited; timothy or other grass hay for adults, alfalfa under a year old), 10% leafy greens and about 5% pellets. Fruit and carrots only as treats; avoid iceberg lettuce and onion. Fresh water always
Needs at least one other bonded rabbit; a neutered male and neutered female is a good pairing
Prey animals that startle easily; handle gently and calmly, since rough handling can cause serious injuries such as spinal fractures
Most active in early morning, late afternoon and overnight
notes: Rabbits chew everything; give hay, cardboard and safe chew toys.
